- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative mid-horizon, model should adjust downward gradually, not abruptly.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), forecast should not assume continuation of trend — bias toward prior mean.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model should not over-forecast peak — cap maximum deviation at +10% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending, forecast should not diverge more than 5% from 14-day moving average.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true outcome by 3–5% in early periods, reduce early forecast weights by 10–15% to avoid lagged bias.
